builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: What Transfers Across Protein Pockets? Experience Reuse in Molecular Optimization for Agentic Structure-Based Drug Design
summary: This technique replaces the repeated, expensive docking of speculative edits by ranking an agent's proposed molecular edits against a reusable log of historical outcomes. The cost is the ongoing maintenance of this base and the engineering needed to define and query keys across different protein pockets. A critical failure mode is that keys which transfer to unseen pockets primarily describe the edit and molecule, not the target, so the base may fail to separate good from bad edits for novel biology.
rationale: The core idea of reusing an agent's own history to rank proposals is implementable within the reader's constraints, but the abstract explicitly notes that target-specific signals do not transfer to unseen pockets, making its effectiveness for new workloads uncertain and requiring validation on their specific use cases.
technique: Cross-pocket experience base for LLM molecular agents

The abstract states that a key using contacts, action, and round sharply separates improving from worsening edits within a base built from a single run, and that naming the target separates them several times more sharply. It makes no claim about transfer to unseen pockets and provides no numerical factor.
